reasons.reader_question: The ladder strikes mid-learning, so the reader leaves asking whether the newly bound pairs can fight. Pair-specific dread lands, especially Kuttu and Bhaskaran.
reasons.change: Neela refuses command, the queen loses the crown leaf, twenty-nine bonds form, and Neela ends up holding eleven leashes she swore off.
reasons.romance_movement: A new reason: she names Devan publicly as chosen, giving the word as freedom. His answer is one touch, plus 'Left side', which pays off chapter 23.
reasons.shown_chemistry: He touches her hand and she turns it into his palm. His flat 'Twenty-eight' and his hand on her shoulder show attunement without narration.
reasons.character_logic: Neela collecting the members' pages right after refusing to hold any has no stated reason. The irony feels arranged rather than chosen.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: Every naming has a price on the page: Bhaskaran's raw fingers, the queen's welt, intake rolls, eleven held pages. The thorn drill makes iron imminent.
reasons.prose: Lines like 'Unseen is owned' are quotable and AI tells are minimal. The page-count paragraph is clotted arithmetic, and 'as if the air had weight' is stock.
reasons.continuity: No conflicts with the bible. Thilak's page in the gate basket, Pavi as otter, Kandan's Mathoor mother and the four unready guards all match.

fixes: At 'On top lay the members' own Resin House pages, handed to her for the dusk', the handover is author-arranged. Give a reason Neela chose at the cairn fire, such as the Company voting that one keeper hold the pages so every burning is seen and counted. Have her agree knowing the risk. Then 'I hold the leash I refused' becomes the cost of her own decision.

At 'Thirty-nine pages had been left to burn, now that Thilak's was gone', the arithmetic stalls the climax. Reduce it to two clean sentences: forty pages, Thilak's already gone, twenty-eight burned, eleven whole under her hand. Cut the restated 'twenty-eight Company names, twenty-eight villages' unless it carries a new image.

At 'crossed to a spear-captain with a scarred chin, a stranger', a crown man with his back to the shelf cannot see her turn. Show him breaking Devan's count-sixty order by turning round to face her, which is a choice with cost. Match his description to F936, or log the change in new-facts.
reader_question: Can the newly bound odiyans and their partners hold the shelf against iron when every cut lands twice?
new_facts_assessment: new-facts is empty, but the draft adds four facts. (1) The heavy-set guard pairs with a scarred-chin spear-captain, while F936 has grey moustache: reconcile or log. (2) Haran's spears face the road, yet a crown captain must watch his guard turn; show him turning by choice. (3) All thirty guards appear present, though F883/F924 put one in Kodiyur; state that she came with the column. (4) Members hand their pages to Neela; log it.
